title: Echo, end to end
description:
Model the whole path of an echo request, from the client through a simulated I/O manager to the driver and back.

```
client: echo "ping" (out 16)
I/O manager: allocates 16-byte system buffer, copies 4 bytes in
driver: echoes 4 bytes, Information 4, STATUS_SUCCESS
I/O manager: copies 4 bytes back
client: got "ping"
bad request (out 2): driver says BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, client reports it
```
hints: The I/O manager is the only part that touches both the client's buffers and the system buffer (lesson 16.10).
Build it from the previous four projects; each layer should be testable alone.
requirements: Three layers as separate functions or classes: client, I/O manager, driver.
Use the IOCTL code, the buffered I/O rules and the validation from the earlier projects.
Print what each layer does, so the flow is visible.
stretch: Write the real driver and client and run them in a virtual machine, following milestone 16's project lesson.
